subject: Mathematics
title: Sets, Relations and Functions
summary: A set is a well-defined collection. Operations — union, intersection, difference, complement — follow De Morgan's laws, and the inclusion–exclusion principle counts elements of unions.
A relation from A to B is any subset of A × B. Relations on a set can be reflexive, symmetric, transitive (all three = equivalence relation, which splits the set into equivalence classes).
A function assigns each element of the domain exactly one image. Functions can be one-one (injective), onto (surjective) or both (bijective); only bijections have inverses.
JEE loves counting questions: number of relations, functions, one-one and onto maps, and reflexive or symmetric relations.

formulas.name: Inclusion–exclusion (2 sets)
formulas.formula: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B)

formulas.name: Inclusion–exclusion (3 sets)
formulas.formula: n(A ∪ B ∪ C) = Σn(A) − Σn(A ∩ B) + n(A ∩ B ∩ C)

formulas.name: Power set
formulas.formula: n(P(A)) = 2ⁿ for n(A) = n;  proper subsets = 2ⁿ − 1

formulas.name: Cartesian product and relations
formulas.formula: n(A × B) = mn;  number of relations from A to B = 2^(mn)

formulas.name: Relations on a set with n elements
formulas.formula: total 2^(n²);  reflexive 2^(n² − n);  symmetric 2^(n(n+1)/2);  reflexive and symmetric 2^(n(n−1)/2)

formulas.name: Equivalence relation
formulas.formula: reflexive (a R a) + symmetric (a R b ⇒ b R a) + transitive (a R b, b R c ⇒ a R c)
formulas.mistake: The empty relation on a non-empty set is symmetric and transitive but not reflexive.

formulas.name: Counting functions (m-set → n-set)
formulas.formula: all functions nᵐ;  one-one nPm (m ≤ n);  onto Σ (−1)ᵏ C(n, k)(n − k)ᵐ (m ≥ n);  bijections n! (m = n)

formulas.name: Even and odd functions
formulas.formula: even f(−x) = f(x) (symmetric about y-axis);  odd f(−x) = −f(x) (symmetric about origin);  every f = even part + odd part

formulas.name: Composition and inverse
formulas.formula: (g∘f)(x) = g(f(x));  (g∘f)⁻¹ = f⁻¹∘g⁻¹;  f⁻¹ exists ⇔ f bijective;  graphs of f and f⁻¹ are mirror images in y = x

formulas.name: Greatest integer and fractional part
formulas.formula: [x] ≤ x < [x] + 1;  {x} = x − [x] ∈ [0, 1);  [x + n] = [x] + n for integer n

formulas.name: Periodic functions
formulas.formula: period of sin, cos = 2π;  tan, cot = π;  {x} = 1;  |sin x| = π;  period of f(ax + b) = T/|a|

examples.title: Union count
examples.problem: In a class 40 students like cricket, 30 like football and 15 like both. How many like at least one?

examples.title: Number of relations
examples.problem: A has 3 elements and B has 4. How many relations from A to B?

examples.title: Functions and one-one functions
examples.problem: A has 3 elements, B has 4. Number of functions and one-one functions from A to B?

examples.title: Onto functions
examples.problem: How many onto functions are there from a 4-element set to a 3-element set?

examples.title: Reflexive and symmetric relations
examples.problem: On a set with 3 elements, how many reflexive relations and how many symmetric relations?

topics.title: Types of sets
topics.explain: Empty (∅), singleton, finite, infinite, equal sets, equivalent sets (same cardinality), subsets, universal set. Intervals: open (a, b), closed [a, b], half-open.

topics.title: Symmetric difference
topics.explain: A Δ B = (A − B) ∪ (B − A) = (A ∪ B) − (A ∩ B). Useful in Venn-diagram questions.

topics.title: Equivalence classes
topics.explain: An equivalence relation on A partitions A into disjoint classes. Example: R = {(a, b): a − b divisible by 3} on integers has three classes — remainders 0, 1, 2.

topics.title: Checking one-one and onto
topics.explain: One-one: f(x₁) = f(x₂) ⇒ x₁ = x₂, or f strictly monotonic; horizontal line test. Onto: range = codomain. A function from a finite set to itself is one-one if and only if it is onto.

topics.title: Range-finding techniques
topics.explain: Write y = f(x) and solve for x, then find conditions on y; use monotonicity, completing the square, or the AM–GM inequality; for rational functions in x² use discriminant ≥ 0.

topics.title: Special functions
topics.explain: Modulus |x|, signum sgn x (1, 0, −1), greatest integer [x], fractional part {x}, exponential and logarithmic functions. Know their graphs, domains and ranges.
